title: Lime Posset
subtitle: Three ingredients, cream, sugar, lime, set by citrus acid alone
excerpt: Double cream boiled with sugar, then sharp lime juice stirred in, the acid sets the cream without any gelatine. Pour into glasses and chill for 3 hours.
sourceNotes: Posset is one of the oldest British desserts, originally a hot drink of milk curdled with wine or ale. The modern version, cream set by citric acid, appears in British cooking from the late 20th century and is now a restaurant staple for its simplicity and reliable result. The lemon version is the most traditional; lime gives a more tropical, vivid flavour.

recipe.batchNotes: Scales up easily, double or triple the quantities and pour into more glasses.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 2 days ahead and keep covered in the fridge. The set improves slightly by day two.

content.text: Lime posset sets by a simple chemical reaction, the citric acid in fresh lime juice denatures the cream proteins, causing the mixture to thicken and hold without any gelatine or eggs. The result is a smooth, clean-tasting set cream with a bright, sharp edge and a rich, mousse-like texture. Boiling the cream with sugar concentrates it slightly; the lime juice goes in off the heat. Pour into glasses and chill for 3 hours.

items.prepNote: from about 5 limes, freshly squeezed, or substitute lemon juice for a classic lemon posset

content.text: Pour the double cream and caster sugar into a medium saucepan. Bring to the boil over a medium heat, stirring to dissolve the sugar. Once boiling, set a timer and boil for exactly 3 minutes, stirring frequently and watching that it does not boil over. The cream will thicken slightly and reduce a little.

Remove the pan from the heat. Add the lime juice and stir well for 30 seconds, you will notice the mixture thickening slightly as the acid reacts with the cream. Pour through a fine sieve into a jug, then divide between 4 to 6 glasses or ramekins. Leave to cool at room temperature for 20 minutes, then cover with cling film and refrigerate for at least 3 hours until set.

items.symptom: Posset has not set after 3 hours
items.cause: Too little citrus juice, or the cream was not boiled for long enough.
items.fix: The juice quantity is critical, 80ml is the minimum for 600ml of cream. Check the posset is properly cold before concluding it has not set; a barely cold posset will feel runny. Leave for a further hour. Next time, boil the cream for the full 3 minutes.

items.cause: The citrus juice was added too quickly or when the cream was too hot.
items.fix: Remove the pan fully from the heat and wait 30 seconds before adding the juice. Stir steadily as you pour, the texture should be smooth and glossy.

items.cause: Limes vary in sharpness and the sugar level may feel unbalanced with mild citrus.
items.fix: Use 130g sugar next time, or add a further tablespoon of lime juice to balance. Freshly squeezed juice always gives better acidity than bottled.

content.text: Keeps covered in the fridge for up to 3 days. The set firms slightly over time. Serve cold, directly from the fridge. Do not freeze.
